:::{#thm-span-subspace}
#### A span is a subspace

For any vectors $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k \in \reals^p$,
$\operatorname{span}\cb{\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k}$ (@def-span)
is a subspace of $\reals^p$ (@def-subspace).

:::

::: proof

The span is not empty:
it contains $0 \cd \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + 0 \cd \vecf{v}_k = \vzero$.

**Addition.**
Take two vectors in the span,
$\vecf{u} = a_1 \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + a_k \vecf{v}_k$
and $\vecf{w} = b_1 \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + b_k \vecf{v}_k$.
Then

$$
\ba
\vecf{u} + \vecf{w}
&= (a_1 \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + a_k \vecf{v}_k)
 + (b_1 \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + b_k \vecf{v}_k)
&& \text{(substitute the two combinations)}
\\
&= (a_1 + b_1)\,\vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + (a_k + b_k)\,\vecf{v}_k
&& \text{(regroup, and distribute each } \vecf{v}_i \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is a linear combination of $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k$,
so it is in the span.

**Scalar multiplication.**
For $c \in \reals$,

$$
\ba
c\,\vecf{u}
&= c\,(a_1 \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + a_k \vecf{v}_k)
&& \text{(substitute the combination)}
\\
&= (c a_1)\,\vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + (c a_k)\,\vecf{v}_k
&& \text{(distribute } c \text{ over the sum)}
\ea
$$

which is again in the span.

:::
